title: Commitment guardrails and contested-resource arbitrator
creator: Lina Park
description:
Problem: As we scale Dedicated and Private sales, multiple initiatives are regularly competing for the same constrained engineering capacity (GPU reservations, infra migration slices, and runtime-optimization cycles). Without clear guardrails, product teams over-commit leading to missed milestones, degraded SLOs, and ad-hoc prioritization that bypasses finance and reliability constraints.

Goal: Define a lightweight, repeatable playbook plus an automated 'Contested Resource Arbitrator' evaluation flow that: (1) surfaces contested capacity across initiatives, (2) enforces commitment guardrails (minimum runway, critical-path ownership, measurable deliverables), and (3) provides a deterministic escalation path for trade-offs. Playbook must be adopted by PMs, Eng leads, and Finance for Q1 planning.

Scope: Company-level OKR alignment + cross-functional initiative intake and capacity arbitration. Includes: a) definition of commitment tiers (Committed, Scoped, Contingent), b) capacity accounting template for initiative owners, c) arbitration rules and decision matrix, d) automation prototype that flags conflicts in the roadmap dashboard (Console + OKR registry), e) templates for canary/quarantine windows for risky initiatives.

Out of scope: Detailed per-repo CI changes, low-level scheduler changes to runtime kernels (handled in ENG tickets), and contractual amendments to existing Reserved Capacity customers.
acceptance_criteria: A published Commitment Guardrails playbook (Markdown in Confluence) with examples and a one-page decision matrix
A Contested Resource Arbitrator runbook implemented as a checklist that PMs and Eng leads use during planning
Automated detection prototype that ingests initiative capacity estimates and flags >2 initiatives contending for the same capacity slice within a 60-day window (dashboard alert exists)
Two pilot initiatives run through the arbitrator flow with documented outcomes and retro notes
Stakeholder sign-off from Eng Infra, Finance, and Head of Product recorded in the Confluence doc
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Nov-Dec): Define tiers, templates, and decision matrix; socialize with Eng and Finance. Phase 2 (Jan): Build detection prototype that reads the OKR registry and roadmap CSV; run two pilots. Phase 3 (Feb): Iterate on rules based on pilots and integrate alerts into Console (beta). Phase 4 (Mar): Full roll-out and inclusion in quarterly planning cadence.
notes: Data sources to use: roadmap CSV export, console-token-latency dashboard, Dedicated capacity reservation ledger
Key stakeholders: Eng Infra (for capacity semantics), Finance (for cost/commitment trade-offs), Legal (for customer contract checks where needed)
Template location: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OKR/Commitment+Guardrails (placeholder until doc is final)
Roadmap CSV schema: initiative_id, owner, committed_gpu_weeks, start_date, end_date, risk_level
